headline: Utilities discussed 120 double poles in Somerville, and two requests on the issue were kept pending.
summary: Eversource and Verizon jointly own the poles, and Verizon said it has no double poles in the city that need its action. Councilors raised concerns about leaning poles and wires touching traffic lights, and Comcast, Xfinity, and Astound did not respond to an invitation. A public comment on double poles was recommended to be marked work completed.
decisions: Accepted the minutes of the June 29, 2026 meeting, 3-0.
Recommended marking the public comment on utility double poles as work completed.
Kept resolution 26-0628 on monitoring double poles and abandoned wires in committee.
Kept resolution 26-0627 on utility plans for double poles in committee.

## City of Somerville, Massachusetts City Council Sustainability and Infrastructure Committee Meeting Minutes

Monday, October 26, 2026

6:00 PM

This meeting was held via Zoom and was called to order by Chair Clingan at 6:01 p.m. and adjourned at 7:57 p.m. on a Roll Call Vote of 3 in favor (Councilors Scott, Hardt and Clingan), 0 opposed, 0 absent.

Also present: Kevin Klein - Interim Director of Inspectional Services Department, Amanda Nagim-Williams - Director of Intergovernmental Affairs, Jason Wright - Eversource Senior Community Relations Specialist, Tatum Kelleher - Verizon Director of State and Local Government Affairs, Eric Weisman - Department of Public Works Commissioner, Brian Postlewaite - Director of Engineering and Delaney Fisher-Cassiol - Clerk of Committees

3. Resolution

By Councilor Hardt and Councilor Scott

(ID # 26-0628 ) That the Commissioner of Public Works and the Director of Infrastructure

and Asset Management appear before this Council to discuss the process of monitoring progress on addressing double poles and abandoned wires, with

the goal of eliminating the potential hazards, tree damage, and nuisances associated with both.

This item was discussed with item #26-0627.

RESULT: KEPT IN COMMITTEE

4. Resolution

By Councilor Hardt and Councilor Scott

(ID # 26-0627 ) That representatives from Eversource, National Grid, Comcast, Xfinity, Astound, and Verizon appear before this Council to discuss plans for

addressing double poles and abandoned wires, with the goal of eliminating the potential hazards, tree damage, and nuisances associated with both.

- Jason Wright, Eversource Senior Community Relations Specialist, noted

that the National Joint Utilities Notification System (NJUNS) is used to track poles in the city. He stated that there are 120 double poles in

- Somerville and that the poles are jointly owned by Eversource and Verizon.

- Councilor Scott asked whose responsibility it is to enter information into

NJUNS, and Specialist Wright confirmed that Eversource submits the information.

Tatum Kelleher, Verizon Director of State and Local Government Affairs, noted that Verizon and Eversource are joint pole owners. Communication

wires are typically at the bottom of the pole, so Verizon tends to be the last to transfer its wires to the new poles. Eversource's equipment is at the top, so it generally initiates the process. Specialist Wright noted that Eversource and Verizon started an agreement last year under which Eversource sets the new

pole and Verizon removes the old one, which has improved efficiency. He explained that no single company controls all attachments on a pole, so the timing depends on multiple parties. Double poles occur for various reasons, including damage and transformer upgrades. When a second pole is

installed, utilities try to transfer the wiring at the time of installation, but sometimes this requires an outage so it cannot be completed immediately.

- Councilor Hardt asked whether there is a plan to address the double poles in
- the city and what rate of progress is expected. Specialist Wright noted that

Eversource has standing meetings with its engineering team and that the city has been a helpful partner in prioritizing poles. Eversource also has standing meetings with Verizon. Brian Postlewaite, Director of Engineering, noted

that his team primarily handles major construction projects involving streetscapes and utility work and he stated that Eversource and Verizon have

been cooperative partners. Eric Weisman, DPW Commissioner, noted that pole requests have generally been escalated due to health and safety

- concerns and echoed that Eversource and Verizon have been good partners.

- Director Kelleher noted that Verizon tries to complete transfers within 30

days and does not currently have any double poles in Somerville that require action on their part. As other utilities move their lines to the new poles, the remaining work enters Verizon's system for completion. Councilor Hardt

noted that Comcast and RCN are among the biggest offenders when it comes to delays in transferring utility wires. Specialist Wright explained that some poles Eversource originally had planned to remove became Verizon's

- responsibility under the new agreement. Chair Clingan noted that Comcast

Xfinity and Astound did not respond to his invitation to attend the meeting, potentially due to outdated contacts.

- Councilor Scott highlighted several specific poles of concern, including

some which are dangerously leaning and have wires touching city traffic lights. Specialist Wright offered to connect with Councilor Scott about the specific poles. Chair Clingan asked whether there is a street-view platform

to see what the poles look like in real-time. Specialist Wright noted that there are no photos available, but Eversource has a map of the poles and infrastructure. Somerville resident Chris Dwan noted that the double poles

on Ivaloo Street have been resolved, but there seems to be a gap between the people who assure residents that work will be completed and the people who

actually complete the work. Dwan noted that this has been frustrating and has caused a loss of trust.

- Councilor Scott expressed concern that double poles remain despite a state

law requiring their removal within 90 days and noted that there is a workflow issue. Councilor Hardt emphasized the need for an improved

workflow and a set process. Chair Clingan asked for specific goals and next steps. Director Kelleher noted that Verizon and Eversource proactively

- established their agreement and have seen increased efficiency as a result.

- She added that utilities sometimes depend on residents to report issues
- because residents are more familiar with conditions in their neighborhoods.

- In response to a question from Councilor Hardt, Eversource agreed to share

a contact for Comcast. Chair Clingan expressed interest in developing a shared game plan among the utility companies.

RESULT: KEPT IN COMMITTEE
